confidence: Moderate confidence in bottle-to-glass mechanism, low confidence in culprit. Official mixture and band evidence link objects; person-specific route and trace findings are missing.
plausibility_notes: Return counter outside solid wall versus visitor doorway is a clear, playable distinction between ordinary document collection and bottle access.
The exhaustive assertion that staff never passed bottle or contents through the slot feels authored to close alternate routes, although useful for fair deduction.
Matching mixture and original-band scrap inside glass strengthen a two-stage mechanism: acquire poison during exposure, then contaminate glass. They do not identify a person.
Band scrap reaching glass is possible through a makeshift carrier; the actual transfer mechanism still needs evidence. Direct pouring might instead leave band on bottle.
Visual items are captions and identifiers here; physical fit and photographic legibility cannot be assessed.
Securing belongings after death is coherent. Official findings must be distinguished clearly from owners' explanations; correction supplies that distinction.
Four late-first-entry claims now matter but remain unverified without logs or an innocent-truth rule.
Exposing live poison under donor pressure remains the largest behavioral contrivance.
Audit retains earlier correction: no glass security cover, Hugh retains emptied envelope, Method excerpts are official findings followed by personal explanations.
